fields.meta_title: Retail Survey Builder That Compares Stores | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a retail survey that tags every answer with its store number and shows which location needs attention. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Retail Survey That Compares Every Store
fields.hero_description: Get a retail survey for shoppers and store staff, with every answer tagged by store and saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts Behind a Retail Survey
fields.features_subheading: The first three shape what a shopper or associate sees. The last three decide where each answer goes and who hears about it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from one prompt

Describe your stores, who answers, and what each answer should change. Emergent writes the survey and its database from that prompt, and one more sentence edits any question.
fields.feature_2:
A store number on every answer

Each store gets its own QR code and link, so every answer arrives tagged with the store it came from. Compare one location with the rest in a single table, with no sorting by hand.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Shoppers scan the code at the register and answer one question per screen. Associates answer on their own phones during a break, and the survey puts no cap on how many respond.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts to the manager who can fix it

Set a line for any score. When an answer falls under it, the app emails that store's manager or posts in Slack, and the district manager sees the same alert in the app.
fields.feature_5:
Answers in a database you own

Every answer is a row in a database you own, with its store, date, and question. Put this quarter's scores beside last quarter's, or sync the table with your point-of-sale API.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Put the survey on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep a copy there.

fields.tab_content_1:
Slow checkout shows up at one of 6 stores

Wexby Hardware prints a QR code on every receipt, and each code opens a 3-question survey tagged with its store. In April, 1,284 shoppers answer across 6 stores. The Route 9 store rates checkout speed 2.8 out of 5, the lowest of the 6. The regional manager adds a Saturday morning cashier there.
fields.tab_content_2:
Managers hear by email when a visit falls under 16 of 20

A district manager at Sorrelwick Pet Supply walks each store with a 20-item checklist on her phone. Any store that scores under 16 sends its manager an email listing every missed item. In June, the Dunlin store scores 14 of 20, and its manager gets the 6 missed items to fix before the next visit.
fields.tab_content_3:
After a May change, only 9 of 24 agree on schedules

Every other Friday, Kestly Outfitters asks associates 3 questions and saves no names with the answers. One reads: I get my schedule 2 weeks ahead. At the Larch Avenue store, 19 of 24 agreed in April. After a May scheduling change, 9 of 24 agree, and the manager goes back to posting schedules 2 weeks out.
fields.tab_content_4:
For 41 shoppers, oat milk was the missing item

Shoppers at the Fallowby Market service desk scan a sign asking what they could not find. In March, 312 requests come in. At month end, the app posts the 5 most requested items to the grocery team's channel in Slack. Unsweetened oat milk leads with 41 shoppers, and the buyer adds it to the next order.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Retail Survey Across Your Stores
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a retail survey, tag every answer by store, and send each result to the person who acts on it.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the decision the survey feeds, such as staffing a register on Saturdays or reordering a product. Any question that cannot change a decision comes out. For a first round, keep it to 3 to 5 questions for each audience.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Shoppers and associates see a store from different sides, so give each group its own survey and its own prompt. Tell Emergent which fields every answer carries, such as the store number and the department.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set up a separate QR code and link for every location before anyone answers, and print the store number next to each receipt code. An answer tagged after the fact is a guess, and guesses break the comparison between stores.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A shopper answers while walking to the car. Ask one rating, one yes or no, and one open box. Use the same 5-point scale at every store and in every month, and this April lines up against last April.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the alert lines in advance
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which score counts as a problem before the first answer arrives, and who hears about it. A store manager can fix a low checkout score this week; a regional manager needs the pattern across stores.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Pilot the survey in one store
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run it in one store for a week. Scan the code from a real receipt, answer on an older phone, and confirm each answer lands in the database with the right store number before the other locations get their codes.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Tell associates what changed because of their answers, and post one line near the register for shoppers. People answer the next round when the last one led somewhere. Then compare stores month over month and adjust the questions.

faq_plan.a: A retail survey is a short questionnaire a store or chain sends to shoppers or its own staff about how its stores run. Because each answer is tied to a store, results compare across locations, down to checkout speed at one register or a gap on one shelf.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a retail survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: who answers, which store each answer belongs to, and what should happen to a low score. Emergent builds the survey and its database, and you change any question with one more sentence. Test it in one store before the rest get their codes.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a retail survey ask shoppers?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the parts of the visit a store can change: how long checkout took, whether staff helped, whether the shopper found what they came for, and how clean the store was. Add one open question, such as what nearly made them leave without buying. Skip demographic questions unless a decision depends on them.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a retail survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep a shopper survey to 3 to 5 questions, short enough to finish on the way to the car. A store visit checklist can run longer, around 20 items, because a district manager fills it in as part of the job. Keep an associate pulse to 3 or 4 questions every two weeks.

faq_plan.q: How do I get in-store shoppers to take a retail survey?
faq_plan.a: Put the survey where the shopper already is: a QR code printed on the receipt, a sign at the service desk, or a link in the emailed receipt. Say how long it takes, such as 3 questions, and make the first screen a single tap. Thank them on the last screen and tell them what the store will do with the answers.

faq_plan.q: How do I compare retail survey results across store locations?
faq_plan.a: Tag each answer with its store when it is collected, through a separate QR code or link per location, rather than asking shoppers which store they visited. Then compare the same question on the same scale across stores and months. A survey built with Emergent keeps each response, with its store and date, in a database you own, ready to sort by location.

faq_plan.q: Should a retail employee survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for questions about managers or pay. Save no name with each answer, state that in the invitation, and show results only for groups of five or more associates. That way no single person can be picked out. Track who has answered separately if you want reminders to stop.

faq_plan.q: What should a retail survey for store visits include?
faq_plan.a: List the checks a district manager can confirm on the floor in one visit: stocked endcaps, shelf tags, clean fitting rooms, a staffed register, and posted safety signs. Score each item pass or miss, set the passing line before the first visit, and add a comment box for anything the list does not cover.

faq_plan.q: How often should a retail survey go out to shoppers?
faq_plan.a: Run a receipt survey all year and review it by store each month. Send longer shopper surveys, such as one about a remodel or new hours, once or twice a year. Surveys built with Emergent have no response caps, and an always-on receipt survey keeps collecting through the busiest month.

faq_plan.q: Can a retail survey pull data from a point-of-sale system?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the point-of-sale system has an API. A survey app built with Emergent can connect to it and sync data in and out, such as adding the order total or register number to each answer. Check that your system's plan includes API access before you build.

plan.angle: Template sites list generic retail questions and stop at the form. This page treats a retail survey as an operating tool for stores: every answer carries its store number, so a chain sees which location is slipping. It covers the four surveys a store team runs (receipt surveys for shoppers, district manager visit audits, associate pulse checks and requests for items the shelf did not have), each built from a prompt into an app with a database the retailer owns and alerts to the person who acts. Satisfaction scoring theory stays on the customer satisfaction page; after-checkout ecommerce questions stay on the post purchase page.
